source_prompt: Ok next item, we need to figure out how to get assistant to keep using dry method outside of planned docs.

current_docs_observations.summary: Plans/DRY_Rules.md is explicitly scoped to anti-drift rules for plan documents, including SSOT references and ContractRef gating.
current_docs_observations.risk: If this remains the only explicit DRY definition, implementers may treat non-Plan assistant outputs as outside scope.

current_docs_observations.summary: Plans/agent-rules-context.md already says project-level rules such as `Always use DRY Method` apply to every agent that works on that project, and both Application and Project rules flow through a single rules pipeline.
current_docs_observations.risk: This creates a good implementation route, but it does not by itself define what DRY adherence means for non-Plan output artifacts.

current_docs_observations.summary: The single rules pipeline and Instruction Bundle route already covers Assistant, Interview, Orchestrator, and delegated child runs, and forbids copy-paste of rules into multiple prompt builders.
current_docs_observations.risk: The future compile should extend semantics through this route rather than inventing a separate Assistant-only DRY source.

current_docs_observations.summary: Assistant Chat already has deterministic bundle ordering and an Injected Context visibility requirement that can host rules/DRY disclosure without creating a separate visible model.
current_docs_observations.risk: The existing UI could show context contents but still fail to indicate DRY owner/source checks unless that state is specified.

current_docs_observations.summary: Assistant/Interview generated content already mentions DRY Method enforcement for documentation and plans, but the user request asks for assistant behavior outside planned docs too.
current_docs_observations.risk: Generated non-Plan artifacts such as scripts, code, tests, README content, and config could still duplicate owners unless covered explicitly.

initial_candidate_shape.delivery_mechanism: Existing single rules pipeline plus deterministic Instruction Bundle.
initial_candidate_shape.behavior_surface: Assistant chat answers, code edits, generated files, scripts, tests, READMEs, config, runtime prompts, document builders, Interview, Orchestrator, and delegated child-agent work.
core_behavior: Identify owner artifact/module/schema/config/component before canonical claims or mutations when one exists.
Reuse existing helpers, components, schemas, enums, event names, settings, storage keys, and owner definitions.
Distinguish source-of-truth, projection, summary, compatibility-only, and source-lineage material.
Carry owner refs in generated non-Plan artifacts where that prevents drift.
open_decisions: Whether DRY Method is default application-level, project-level only, or both.
Whether unresolved owner/source routes block mutation or only warn.
Whether visible Assistant Chat DRY/rules evidence is always compactly shown or only surfaced on degraded trust states.

negative_constraints: Do not write canonical Plans during this ledger-only turn.
Do not solve by copy-pasting `DRY Method` into multiple prompt builders.
Do not create a shadow instruction source that the runtime rules pipeline does not read.
Do not limit DRY Method to canonical Plans prose if Jared wants assistant behavior outside planned docs.
Do not create WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or PlanUnit indexes from this planning item.
